The community revolves around the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy #123 456 789, owned by and insuring Jane Sample. The policy includes provisions such as the Living Benefit, Death Benefit, and Waiver of Premiums Benefit, and is governed by TD Life, with Quebec's Civil Code influencing spousal beneficiary designations. Key documents like the Privacy Agreement and Health Question Confirmation are part of the Policy Package. The community involves clear legal and contractual relationships that define the policy's operation and impact.

## Central role of Jane Sample as policyholder and insured

Jane Sample is the pivotal figure in this community, serving as both the policy owner and the insured under the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy #123 456 789. Her actions and status directly affect the policy's validity and operation, such as premium payments and beneficiary designations. As the insured, her death triggers the death benefit payout, making her life and health central to the contract's purpose. The policy is effective from January 1, 2023, and renews automatically until her 80th birthday, indicating a long-term financial commitment. Additionally, her personal information is detailed, including date of birth and address, which are essential for identifying her and processing claims. The policy's provisions, such as the Living Benefit, are available to her under specific conditions, further emphasizing her central role. [Data: Entities (4, 6); Relationships (3, 127)]

## Comprehensive provisions of the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy

The TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy encompasses several key benefits and conditions that define its scope and impact. The Death Benefit ensures a sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus outstanding premiums, but excludes suicide within 2 years of coverage. The Living Benefit allows acceleration of up to 50% of the Death Benefit (max $100,000) if the insured is diagnosed with a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. The Waiver of Premiums Benefit, if selected, waives monthly premiums during total disability. These provisions are integral to the policy and are governed by specific conditions, providing financial security but also introducing complexities in claims processing. The policy's automatic renewal every 20 years until age 80 ensures ongoing coverage but may require continued premium payments. [Data: Entities (6, 10, 11, 12, 33); Relationships (12, 13, 14, 39, 40, 42)]

## Legal and beneficiary designations influenced by Quebec's Civil Code

Quebec's Civil Code plays a significant role in shaping beneficiary designations under the policy, particularly regarding spousal rights. In Quebec, a spouse is automatically deemed an irrevocable beneficiary unless expressly designated as revocable, and any designation of a spouse as beneficiary is irrevocable unless specified otherwise. The Civil Code also sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, affecting how long parties have to file legal claims. These legal nuances are critical for policyholders and beneficiaries, as they determine the distribution of proceeds and the ability to change beneficiaries. The Estate option allows proceeds to be distributed according to intestacy laws if no will exists, highlighting the importance of proper estate planning. These provisions reflect Quebec's distinct legal framework and its impact on the policy's administration. [Data: Entities (51, 89); Relationships (68, 133)]

## Policy documentation and privacy practices

The Policy Package includes essential documents such as the Privacy Agreement and Health Question Confirmation. The Privacy Agreement outlines how TD Insurance handles personal information, ensuring transparency and informing policyholders of their rights regarding data collection, use, and disclosure. The Health Question Confirmation contains the policyholder's responses to health questions, which must be accurate as they affect insurability and could impact claim outcomes. These documents are part of the contractual agreement and are provided to the policyholder for review and retention. The Privacy Agreement's relationship with TD Insurance underscores the insurer's obligations to protect personal data, while the Health Question Confirmation is crucial for underwriting and risk assessment. Together, they form the administrative and compliance backbone of the policy. [Data: Entities (7, 8, 60); Relationships (15, 16, 82)]

## Roles and relationships of TD Life and TD Insurance

TD Life is the insurance company that processes change of beneficiary requests and provides the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance policy. It has a direct relationship with Jane Sample as the insured and with the policy itself. Additionally, TD Insurance is mentioned in the Privacy Agreement as the entity handling personal information, indicating a broader corporate structure. The Civil Code of Quebec sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, highlighting the legal environment in which TD Life operates. These entities are central to the policy's administration, from underwriting to claims processing and privacy compliance. Their roles are defined by contractual and legal obligations, ensuring the policy's functionality and regulatory adherence. [Data: Entities (88, 7); Relationships (16, 68, 127, 133)]

## Key policy provisions: 30-Day Review Period and Terminal Illness

The 30-Day Review Period grants Jane Sample the right to cancel the policy within 30 days of the effective date for a full premium refund, providing a safeguard against unsuitable coverage. Terminal Illness is a critical condition that qualifies the insured for the Living Benefit, requiring a diagnosis with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. These provisions are designed to protect the policyholder's interests and offer flexibility in dire circumstances. The review period ensures informed consent, while the terminal illness provision provides financial relief during terminal illness. Both are integral to the policy's consumer protection features and are clearly defined in the policy terms. [Data: Entities (9, 33); Relationships (17, 39)]

## Death Benefit calculation and exclusions

The Death Benefit is the sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus any outstanding premiums. However, no benefit is payable if death results from suicide within 2 years of the effective date or reinstatement, in which case premiums paid are refunded. This exclusion is standard in life insurance policies to mitigate adverse selection. The benefit is payable when a claim is made within 365 days of death, emphasizing the need for timely claims. The interplay between the Death Benefit, Sum Insured, and Suicide exclusion defines the financial outcomes for beneficiaries and highlights the importance of policy conditions. [Data: Entities (12, 29, 34); Relationships (40, 42)]

## Estate as a beneficiary designation option

The Estate option allows proceeds to be paid to the estate and distributed according to intestacy laws if no will exists. This designation is important for policyholders without named beneficiaries, as it ensures proceeds are handled through the legal system. The relationship between Estate and TD Life indicates that TD Life facilitates such distributions. This option underscores the need for estate planning and the potential legal complexities if no will is present. It also highlights the policy's flexibility in beneficiary designations and the importance of clear instructions. [Data: Entities (89); Relationships (133)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

3|TD Life Insurance Policy Premium and Lapse Provisions|"# TD Life Insurance Policy Premium and Lapse Provisions

The community centers on the policy administration of TD Life Insurance Company, specifically the provisions related to premium payments, grace periods, policy lapse, and reinstatement. Key entities include the Policy Schedule, Premium, Grace Period, Policy Lapse, and Reinstatement. These entities are interconnected: the Policy Schedule specifies the First Premium Due Date; premiums must be paid by that date to maintain coverage; failure to pay within the Grace Period results in Policy Lapse; and Reinstatement is the process to restore a lapsed policy, requiring payment of unpaid premiums and evidence of insurability. The community is fundamental to insurance operations, ensuring clarity and enforceability of contractual terms.

## Policy Schedule defines key dates and terms

The Policy Schedule is the foundational document that specifies the First Premium Due Date and other policy details. It is part of TD Life Insurance Company policies, indicating its central role in policy issuance and administration. The Policy Schedule ensures that policyholders are aware of their obligations, particularly the timing of premium payments, which is crucial for maintaining coverage. Its degree of 4 suggests multiple relationships with other entities, such as the First Premium Due Date and Premium. [Data: Entities (31); Relationships (72)]

## Premiums are due by specified dates and impact benefits

Premiums are payments due to the insurer by the due date, payable monthly or annually. They may be eligible for a discount, but unpaid premiums reduce the death benefit and accumulate interest on the living benefit. The First Premium Due Date, specified in the Policy Schedule, is when the first premium is due. This entity has a high degree (7), indicating its importance and multiple connections to other entities like Grace Period and Policy Lapse. [Data: Entities (30, 27); Relationships (45)]

## Grace period provides temporary coverage continuation

The Grace Period is a thirty-calendar-day window during which the policy remains in effect even if premiums are not paid by the due date. This provision gives policyholders additional time to submit payments without losing coverage. However, if premiums remain unpaid by the end of the grace period, the policy lapses, ending all coverage. This mechanism balances flexibility for policyholders with the insurer's need for timely payments. The Grace Period is linked to Premium and Policy Lapse. [Data: Entities (26); Relationships (43, 44)]

## Policy lapse occurs after non-payment within grace period

A policy lapse happens when the policy ends because outstanding premiums are not paid by the end of the thirty-day grace period. This is a critical event that terminates coverage and may require reinstatement to restore benefits. The relationship between Premium and Policy Lapse highlights the consequence of non-payment. Lapse is a key risk for policyholders and a factor in policy management. [Data: Entities (25); Relationships (44)]

## Reinstatement restores a lapsed policy under conditions

Reinstatement is the process of restoring a lapsed policy as described in the section 'Putting your policy back into effect'. It is subject to criteria: the insured person must be alive, unpaid premiums must be paid, a completed Reinstatement Application must be submitted, and new evidence of insurability may be required. The Reinstatement Effective Date is when the policy is reinstated. This process provides a pathway for policyholders to regain coverage after a lapse, but it involves strict requirements. [Data: Entities (23, 24); Relationships (34, 36)]

## Interconnection of entities ensures policy integrity

The entities within this community are tightly interconnected: the Policy Schedule specifies the First Premium Due Date; Premium payments are due by that date; failure to pay within the Grace Period leads to Policy Lapse; and Reinstatement allows restoration after fulfilling conditions. This network of relationships ensures that the insurance policy operates within a clear framework, protecting both the insurer and the policyholder. 5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

## General provisions

After insurance has been in effect for two (2) years from the effective date or reinstatement effective date we will treat all of the answers you gave as evidence of insurability as true, except for cases of fraudulent misrepresentation. ## Waiver

We shall not be deemed to have waived or changed any condition of this policy , either in whole or in part, unless such waiver or change is clearly expressed in writing and signed by an officer of TD Life Insurance Company. Legal Action No action at law or in equity shall be brought to recover on the policy prior to the expiration of 120 days after proof of claim has been furnished in accordance with the requirements of the policy . Every action or proceeding against an insurer for the recovery of insurance money payable under the contract is absolutely barred unless commenced within the time set out in the Insurance Act (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Alberta and British Columbia), the Insurance Act (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Manitoba), the Limitations Act, 2002 (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Ontario), or other applicable legislation. For those actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Quebec, the prescriptive period is set out in the Civil Code of Quebec . Applicable Laws Your insurance will be governed by the laws of the province where you were resident when you initially applied for insurance under this policy , without reference to that province's rules about conflicts of laws. English Language It is the express wish of the parties that this policy and all related documents, including notices and other communications, be drawn up in the English language only. SAMPLE

## Waiver of Premiums Benefit

This section is applicable if you selected the Waiver of Premiums Benefit when you applied for TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance.

## Waiver of Premiums on total disability

If while this policy is in effect, and before the insured person's 65th birthday, the insured person becomes totally disabled , as defined below, and remains totally disabled for a continuous period of six months, we will:

- Automatically change the policy premium payment frequency to monthly, if the payment frequency is other than monthly, beginning with the date we agree to waive premiums. If after the end of the period of total disability , you wish to pay premiums other than monthly then you must notify us .
- Waive the payment of monthly premiums from the date the insured person becomes totally disabled and for as long as the total disability continues, up to the insured person's 80th birthday.

'Total disability' or 'totally disabled' shall mean that the insured person , as a result of bodily injury or disease, is wholly prevented during the first two years after the injury or the onset of the disease from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation; after the first two years the insured person must be prevented by the injury or disease, from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education or experience.

Definition SAMPLE

## Conversion option exercised during total disability

If you exercise the conversion option in this policy while the insured person is totally disabled , we will not waive premiums for the converted insurance policy .

## Exceptions

## We will not waive premiums if total disability results, either directly or indirectly, from one or more of the following causes:

● Attempted suicide or self-inflicted injury (whether the insured person is aware or not aware of the result of their actions, regardless of the insured person's state of mind); ● War, whether declared or undeclared, any act of war or activities directly related to service in the armed forces of any country; ● The commission or attempted commission by the insured person of a criminal act; ● An accident that occurs while the insured person is operating any kind of conveyance while their blood alcohol level exceeds the legal limit where the accident occurs; ● Taking a drug in a manner other than prescribed by a licensed physician. We must receive notice of total disability while the insured person is alive and continues to be totally disabled . We must also receive proof of the total disability of the insured person within 3 months of the date notice was provided to us . We will not waive any premiums falling due more than 12 months before the insured person gives us notice of total disability . At any time, we may ask for proof that the insured person continues to be totally disabled and, if such proof is not provided, the insured person will be deemed to no longer be totally disabled on the day prior to the date on which we asked for the proof and monthly premiums will begin again. 5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

## Waiver of Premiums on total disability

If while this policy is in effect, and before the insured person's 65th birthday, the insured person becomes totally disabled , as defined below, and remains totally disabled for a continuous period of six months, we will:

- Automatically change the policy premium payment frequency to monthly, if the payment frequency is other than monthly, beginning with the date we agree to waive premiums. If after the end of the period of total disability , you wish to pay premiums other than monthly then you must notify us .
- Waive the payment of monthly premiums from the date the insured person becomes totally disabled and for as long as the total disability continues, up to the insured person's 80th birthday.

'Total disability' or 'totally disabled' shall mean that the insured person , as a result of bodily injury or disease, is wholly prevented during the first two years after the injury or the onset of the disease from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation; after the first two years the insured person must be prevented by the injury or disease, from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education or experience.

The TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy encompasses several key benefits and conditions that define its scope and impact. The Death Benefit ensures a sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus outstanding premiums, but excludes suicide within 2 years of coverage. The Living Benefit allows acceleration of up to 50% of the Death Benefit (max $100,000) if the insured is diagnosed with a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. The Waiver of Premiums Benefit, if selected, waives monthly premiums during total disability. Quebec's Civil Code plays a significant role in shaping beneficiary designations under the policy, particularly regarding spousal rights. In Quebec, a spouse is automatically deemed an irrevocable beneficiary unless expressly designated as revocable, and any designation of a spouse as beneficiary is irrevocable unless specified otherwise. The Civil Code also sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, affecting how long parties have to file legal claims. These legal nuances are critical for policyholders and beneficiaries, as they determine the distribution of proceeds and the ability to change beneficiaries. Terminal Illness is a critical condition that qualifies the insured for the Living Benefit, requiring a diagnosis with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. The Death Benefit is the sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus any outstanding premiums. 5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

## Waiver of Premiums Benefit

This section is applicable if you selected the Waiver of Premiums Benefit when you applied for TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance.

## Waiver of Premiums on total disability

If while this policy is in effect, and before the insured person's 65th birthday, the insured person becomes totally disabled , as defined below, and remains totally disabled for a continuous period of six months, we will:

- Automatically change the policy premium payment frequency to monthly, if the payment frequency is other than monthly, beginning with the date we agree to waive premiums. If after the end of the period of total disability , you wish to pay premiums other than monthly then you must notify us .
- Waive the payment of monthly premiums from the date the insured person becomes totally disabled and for as long as the total disability continues, up to the insured person's 80th birthday.

'Total disability' or 'totally disabled' shall mean that the insured person , as a result of bodily injury or disease, is wholly prevented during the first two years after the injury or the onset of the disease from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation; after the first two years the insured person must be prevented by the injury or disease, from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education or experience.

## Exceptions

● Attempted suicide or self-inflicted injury (whether the insured person is aware or not aware of the result of their actions, regardless of the insured person's state of mind); ● War, whether declared or undeclared, any act of war or activities directly related to service in the armed forces of any country; ● The commission or attempted commission by the insured person of a criminal act; ● An accident that occurs while the insured person is operating any kind of conveyance while their blood alcohol level exceeds the legal limit where the accident occurs; ● Taking a drug in a manner other than prescribed by a licensed physician. We must receive notice of total disability while the insured person is alive and continues to be totally disabled . We must also receive proof of the total disability of the insured person within 3 months of the date notice was provided to us . We will not waive any premiums falling due more than 12 months before the insured person gives us notice of total disability . At any time, we may ask for proof that the insured person continues to be totally disabled and, if such proof is not provided, the insured person will be deemed to no longer be totally disabled on the day prior to the date on which we asked for the proof and monthly premiums will begin again. ## Here are answers to questions you may have about your TD 20-Year Term Life insurance protection

## If my health changes during the term of my coverage, will my premiums increase?

Your premium is set and guaranteed for each 20-year term of your insurance coverage. It will not change during each 20-year term, regardless of changes in your age or health (provided premium payments are made when due and the policy does not lapse ).

No. As long as you continue to pay your premiums, your coverage will automatically renew at the end of each 20-year term for another 20-year term, with no medical questions. Coverage cannot be renewed beyond your 80th birthday. Do I need to re-apply for coverage at the end of each 20-year term? The benefit amount from your insurance will be payable to the beneficiary(ies) you designated. That could be your spouse, child, friend or any other person you selected. Yes, you can convert to a permanent life insurance policy , with no medical questions, at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest the insured's 69th birthday. ## Will my beneficiary(ies) have to pay taxes on the benefit provided by my TD 20-Year Term Life insurance?

No, under current tax law, benefits paid on your insurance are tax-free to the designated beneficiary .

If you are the policy owner , for an additional cost, you may choose to add a Waiver of Premium Benefit to the policy . You would need financial help to protect your lifestyle while you're recovering or retrofit your home, if necessary. The community centers on TD Insurance, a member of TD Bank Group, which offers insurance products and collects, uses, and shares personal information through a network of entities. Key relationships include TD Insurance's connection to TD Life Insurance Company (underwriter of its term life product), its divisions TD Insurance Home and Auto and TD Insurance Travel Medical, and external organizations such as fraud prevention agencies, health care professionals, insurance companies, government agencies, public information data banks, and insurance information bureaus (MIB, LLC and Insurance Bureau of Canada). 5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

## Your right to convert to a permanent life insurance policy

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. The amount of this premium will depend on the age of the insured person at the time the conversion option is exercised, the risk classification used for this policy and the plan of the converted insurance.

The converted policy will not include any waiver of premium benefits that you may have had on this policy .

## Before we will pay any claim under this policy , the person making the claim (the claimant) must provide:

- Proof, satisfactory to us , that the insured person has died;
- Upon our request, access to any medical records that we require to assess the claim, including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report.

In addition, the claimant must provide further proof of claim, if applicable.

In all cases, the proof must be provided within one (1) year of the date of death of the insured person and any cost incurred in providing proof of claim is at the claimant's expense.

## When insurance coverage ends

## All coverage under this policy will end on the earliest of the date when any of the following occurs:

- The insured person dies; or
- We receive request from you to cancel your coverage; or

- The end of the grace period if premiums are not paid; or
- Upon a fraudulent claim made by you or the beneficiary; or
- The insured person's 80th birthday.

We will renew this policy and insurance in effect at the end of the initial 20 year period for successive 20 year renewal periods each of the same length as the initial period, except the renewal anniversary nearest to the insured person's 80th birthday. The final renewal period will only run until the insured person's 80th birthday, at which point the policy will end and there will be no further renewal.

If a benefit is payable, we will pay the benefit to:

- Your beneficiary(ies) ; or
- If there is no beneficiary when the insured person dies, to you or your estate.

The right to name or change the beneficiary designation is reserved to you only. You do not need the consent of any beneficiary or beneficiaries to change any beneficiary under this policy , unless any rule of law requires his or her consent. All beneficiary designations are revocable unless otherwise stated or unless any contrary law applies.

If you wish to name or change your beneficiary , you must submit a written request to us , but such change shall not be binding on us until received at our Head Office. Once the beneficiary change request has been received, it will be our responsibility to fulfill the request as of the date the request was signed, but we will not be responsible for any benefits paid to the previous beneficiary before the receipt of the beneficiary request.

We are not bound by any documents that affect rights under this contract unless the document itself or written notice of it is received at our Head Office. We are not responsible for ensuring that any such document is valid or has the desired effect.

## Premium Adjustments

If incorrect information was provided during the application process that qualified the insured person for preferred rates we reserve the right to re-issue the policy with an adjusted premium based on the correct information.

Any information you provide after the policy's effective date and which impacts the premium can only be honored at time of notification.

## Misstatement of Age and Sex at Birth

If a policy is issued to an insured person based on an incorrect age, the following may apply:

- If the insured person is still eligible for insurance, the premium amount will be adjusted to the correct amount based on the correct date of birth at the insured person's effective date and;
