5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

Fraud prevention agencies and registries are entities that TD Insurance may collect information from and share information with to protect against fraud and financial abuse [Data: Entities (61); Relationships (89)]. The involvement of these entities indicates a robust infrastructure for fraud prevention and data sharing, but it also raises concerns about the accuracy and security of personal information held by third parties.

## Privacy Policy as a governing document

The Privacy Policy is a key entity that governs how TD Insurance handles personal information, including collection, use, sharing, and retention [Data: Entities (59); Relationships (83)]. It is referenced in TD Insurance's description and is central to the community's compliance with privacy regulations. The policy outlines the types of third parties with whom information may be shared and the purposes for such sharing. Given the extensive data-sharing relationships in this community, the Privacy Policy serves as a critical framework for ensuring that personal information is managed appropriately and in accordance with legal requirements. 5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The community revolves around the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy #123 456 789, owned by and insuring Jane Sample. The policy includes provisions such as the Living Benefit, Death Benefit, and Waiver of Premiums Benefit, and is governed by TD Life, with Quebec's Civil Code influencing spousal beneficiary designations. The community involves clear legal and contractual relationships that define the policy's operation and impact.

## Central role of Jane Sample as policyholder and insured

Jane Sample is the pivotal figure in this community, serving as both the policy owner and the insured under the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy #123 456 789. Her actions and status directly affect the policy's validity and operation, such as premium payments and beneficiary designations. As the insured, her death triggers the death benefit payout, making her life and health central to the contract's purpose. The policy is effective from January 1, 2023, and renews automatically until her 80th birthday, indicating a long-term financial commitment. The policy's provisions, such as the Living Benefit, are available to her under specific conditions, further emphasizing her central role. [Data: Entities (4, 6); Relationships (3, 127)]

## Comprehensive provisions of the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy

The TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy encompasses several key benefits and conditions that define its scope and impact. The Death Benefit ensures a sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus outstanding premiums, but excludes suicide within 2 years of coverage. The Living Benefit allows acceleration of up to 50% of the Death Benefit (max $100,000) if the insured is diagnosed with a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. The Waiver of Premiums Benefit, if selected, waives monthly premiums during total disability. These provisions are integral to the policy and are governed by specific conditions, providing financial security but also introducing complexities in claims processing. The policy's automatic renewal every 20 years until age 80 ensures ongoing coverage but may require continued premium payments. [Data: Entities (6, 10, 11, 12, 33); Relationships (12, 13, 14, 39, 40, 42)]

## Legal and beneficiary designations influenced by Quebec's Civil Code

Quebec's Civil Code plays a significant role in shaping beneficiary designations under the policy, particularly regarding spousal rights. In Quebec, a spouse is automatically deemed an irrevocable beneficiary unless expressly designated as revocable, and any designation of a spouse as beneficiary is irrevocable unless specified otherwise. The Civil Code also sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, affecting how long parties have to file legal claims. These legal nuances are critical for policyholders and beneficiaries, as they determine the distribution of proceeds and the ability to change beneficiaries. The Estate option allows proceeds to be distributed according to intestacy laws if no will exists, highlighting the importance of proper estate planning. These provisions reflect Quebec's distinct legal framework and its impact on the policy's administration. [Data: Entities (51, 89); Relationships (68, 133)]

## Policy documentation and privacy practices

The Policy Package includes essential documents such as the Privacy Agreement and Health Question Confirmation. The Privacy Agreement outlines how TD Insurance handles personal information, ensuring transparency and informing policyholders of their rights regarding data collection, use, and disclosure. The Health Question Confirmation contains the policyholder's responses to health questions, which must be accurate as they affect insurability and could impact claim outcomes. These documents are part of the contractual agreement and are provided to the policyholder for review and retention. The Privacy Agreement's relationship with TD Insurance underscores the insurer's obligations to protect personal data, while the Health Question Confirmation is crucial for underwriting and risk assessment. Together, they form the administrative and compliance backbone of the policy. [Data: Entities (7, 8, 60); Relationships (15, 16, 82)]

TD Life is the insurance company that processes change of beneficiary requests and provides the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance policy. It has a direct relationship with Jane Sample as the insured and with the policy itself. Additionally, TD Insurance is mentioned in the Privacy Agreement as the entity handling personal information, indicating a broader corporate structure. The Civil Code of Quebec sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, highlighting the legal environment in which TD Life operates. These entities are central to the policy's administration, from underwriting to claims processing and privacy compliance. Their roles are defined by contractual and legal obligations, ensuring the policy's functionality and regulatory adherence. [Data: Entities (88, 7); Relationships (16, 68, 127, 133)]

## Key policy provisions: 30-Day Review Period and Terminal Illness

The 30-Day Review Period grants Jane Sample the right to cancel the policy within 30 days of the effective date for a full premium refund, providing a safeguard against unsuitable coverage. Terminal Illness is a critical condition that qualifies the insured for the Living Benefit, requiring a diagnosis with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. These provisions are designed to protect the policyholder's interests and offer flexibility in dire circumstances. The review period ensures informed consent, while the terminal illness provision provides financial relief during terminal illness. Both are integral to the policy's consumer protection features and are clearly defined in the policy terms. [Data: Entities (9, 33); Relationships (17, 39)]

## Death Benefit calculation and exclusions

The Death Benefit is the sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus any outstanding premiums. However, no benefit is payable if death results from suicide within 2 years of the effective date or reinstatement, in which case premiums paid are refunded. This exclusion is standard in life insurance policies to mitigate adverse selection. The benefit is payable when a claim is made within 365 days of death, emphasizing the need for timely claims. The interplay between the Death Benefit, Sum Insured, and Suicide exclusion defines the financial outcomes for beneficiaries and highlights the importance of policy conditions. ## Estate as a beneficiary designation option

The Estate option allows proceeds to be paid to the estate and distributed according to intestacy laws if no will exists. This designation is important for policyholders without named beneficiaries, as it ensures proceeds are handled through the legal system. The relationship between Estate and TD Life indicates that TD Life facilitates such distributions. This option underscores the need for estate planning and the potential legal complexities if no will is present. 5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

Your premium is set and guaranteed for each 20-year term of your insurance coverage. It will not change during each 20-year term, regardless of changes in your age or health (provided premium payments are made when due and the policy does not lapse ).

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

The community revolves around the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy #123 456 789, owned by and insuring Jane Sample. ## Central role of Jane Sample as policyholder and insured

Jane Sample is the pivotal figure in this community, serving as both the policy owner and the insured under the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy #123 456 789. Her actions and status directly affect the policy's validity and operation, such as premium payments and beneficiary designations. ## Comprehensive provisions of the TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy

The TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy encompasses several key benefits and conditions that define its scope and impact. The Death Benefit ensures a sum payable to beneficiaries upon Jane Sample's death, calculated as the Sum Insured minus outstanding premiums, but excludes suicide within 2 years of coverage. The Living Benefit allows acceleration of up to 50% of the Death Benefit (max $100,000) if the insured is diagnosed with a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. The Waiver of Premiums Benefit, if selected, waives monthly premiums during total disability. Quebec's Civil Code plays a significant role in shaping beneficiary designations under the policy, particularly regarding spousal rights. In Quebec, a spouse is automatically deemed an irrevocable beneficiary unless expressly designated as revocable, and any designation of a spouse as beneficiary is irrevocable unless specified otherwise. The Civil Code also sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, affecting how long parties have to file legal claims. These legal nuances are critical for policyholders and beneficiaries, as they determine the distribution of proceeds and the ability to change beneficiaries. The Estate option allows proceeds to be distributed according to intestacy laws if no will exists, highlighting the importance of proper estate planning. It has a direct relationship with Jane Sample as the insured and with the policy itself. The Civil Code of Quebec sets the prescriptive period for actions under TD Life contracts, highlighting the legal environment in which TD Life operates. The 30-Day Review Period grants Jane Sample the right to cancel the policy within 30 days of the effective date for a full premium refund, providing a safeguard against unsuitable coverage. Terminal Illness is a critical condition that qualifies the insured for the Living Benefit, requiring a diagnosis with a life expectancy of 12 months or less. ## Waiver of Premiums on total disability

If while this policy is in effect, and before the insured person's 65th birthday, the insured person becomes totally disabled , as defined below, and remains totally disabled for a continuous period of six months, we will:

- Automatically change the policy premium payment frequency to monthly, if the payment frequency is other than monthly, beginning with the date we agree to waive premiums. If after the end of the period of total disability , you wish to pay premiums other than monthly then you must notify us .

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"

5|TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community|"# TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance Policy Community

The community represents a network of entities and relationships related to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy. Key entities include TD (the insurer), the policy owner, the insured person, and the beneficiary. The policy provides life insurance coverage for a 20-year term, with options for conversion to permanent life insurance, and specifies conditions for claims, reinstatement, and beneficiary designations. The Canadian Government is relevant for eligibility requirements (Permanent Resident status). The community is structured around the contractual relationships defined in the policy, with the insured person at the center, given their age and health determine premiums, conversion options, and coverage termination.

## TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance is the central product

The TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy is the core entity in this community, offered by TD Insurance. It provides coverage for a specified 20-year term and is designed to offer financial protection for a defined period. The policy has a sum insured of $181,700.00 in the referenced instance, and coverage begins on September 7, 2023. The policy includes provisions for renewal until the insured turns 80 and conversion to permanent life insurance. This product is the basis for relationships with other entities such as the insured, policy owner, beneficiary, and claimant. [Data: Entities (13); Relationships (102, 99, 116, 117)]

## Roles and responsibilities of policy owner and insured person

The policy owner is the individual or party who holds ownership of the policy, with rights to add optional benefits and designate beneficiaries. The insured person is the individual whose life is covered. Importantly, the policy owner is not necessarily the insured person. The policy owner can change beneficiary designations through a written request, and if the beneficiary is irrevocable, that beneficiary must consent to the payment of a living benefit. The insured person's age, health, and sex assigned at birth affect premiums, conversion options, and coverage eligibility. The insured person's death triggers the payment of the sum insured minus outstanding premiums, and the policy ends. [Data: Entities (21, 20); Relationships (30, 31, 55, 59, 60)]

## Beneficiary designation and rights

A beneficiary is a person or entity designated to receive benefits under the policy upon the insured person's death. The policy owner can choose a spouse, child, friend, or other party as beneficiary. If the beneficiary is irrevocable, that individual must consent to the payment of a living benefit under the policy. The beneficiary designation can typically be changed by the policyholder through a written request. The beneficiary is entitled to receive the tax-free benefit amount from the life insurance policy when the insured passes away. For minor children, a trustee should be named when designating them as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary. [Data: Entities (22, 71, 72, 73, 80, 81); Relationships (31, 104, 105, 118)]

## Claims process and requirements

The claimant is the person making a claim under the policy, required to provide proof of death, medical records, and further proof of claim within one year of the insured person's death. The claimant must provide proof satisfactory to the insurer that the insured person has died, along with further proof of claim if applicable. The insurer may require an attending physician's statement or a coroner's report to assess the claim. The claim process involves providing these documents to the insurer. [Data: Entities (36, 41, 37, 38); Relationships (52, 57, 53, 54)]

## Conversion option and permanent life insurance

The policy owner may convert the term life insurance to a permanent life insurance policy at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the insured person's health. This conversion option provides flexibility and potential long-term coverage. The permanent life insurance policy is the type of insurance the policy owner may convert to. The conversion eligibility is determined by the insured person's 69th birthday. [Data: Entities (32, 40, 74); Relationships (48, 59, 102)]

## Policy termination and renewal terms

All coverage ends on the insured person's 80th birthday, upon which the final renewal period ends and the policy terminates with no further renewal. The insured person's 80th birthday is a key date for policy termination. Additionally, the policy may be reinstated upon a completed Reinstatement Application and new evidence of insurability. The term insurance provides protection for a limited number of years, specifically 20 years, with renewals until age 80. [Data: Entities (45, 39, 28); Relationships (60, 61)]

## Eligibility requirements and Canadian Government involvement

To be eligible for coverage, a proposed insured person must have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government. This requirement links the Canadian Government as an entity in the community. The Canadian Government grants Permanent Resident status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility to apply for insurance coverage under this policy. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (32)]

## Optional benefits: Waiver of Premium

The Waiver of Premium Benefit is an optional add-on to the TD 20-Year Term Life insurance policy that ensures coverage remains in place if the policy owner becomes disabled. This benefit can be added for an additional cost. It provides financial protection by waiving premiums during disability, helping to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (99)]

## Financial protection for children's education

The coverage provides a tax-free lump sum benefit to help cover tuition costs for children's future. Children of the insured may be beneficiaries, and the insurance helps protect their tuition costs and future. A trustee should be named when designating a child or children as Primary or Contingent Beneficiary for minor children. A trustee cannot sign a release of an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation. [Data: Entities (80, 81); Relationships (117, 118)]

## Role of Head Office and beneficiary change requests

Beneficiary change requests and documents affecting rights under the contract must be received at the Head Office to be binding. The Head Office is the central office of the insurance company. This ensures that all changes to beneficiary designations are properly recorded and legally effective. [Data: Entities (35); Relationships (55)]"
